46.e: The thousandeyed Indra served her by providing fire, Kusha grass, sticks for burning, water, fruits, roots and all other things desired by her.

46.sa: गात्रसंवहनश्चैव श्रमापनयनैस्तथा। शक्रस्सर्वेषु कालेषु दितिं परिचचार ह ।।1.46.11।।
46.e: Indra attended on Diti, stroking her limbs gently from time to time to help her regain their  suppleness and alleviate her fatigue.

46.sa: अथ वर्षसहस्रे तु दशोने रघुनन्दन । दिति: परमसम्प्रीता सहस्राक्षमथाब्रवीत्।।1.46.12।।
46.e: O son of the Raghus ten years before completion of a thousand years. Diti, highly pleased with the services rendered by Indra, addressed him", saying:

46.sa: याचितेन सुरश्रेष्ठ तव पित्रा महात्मना। वरो वर्षसहस्रान्ते दत्तो मम सुतं प्रति।।1.46.13।।
46.e: "O best of the gods your illustrious father granted me a boon for a son I sought on completion of a thousand years (of penance).

46.sa: तपश्चरन्त्या वर्षाणि दश वीर्यवतां वर। अवशिष्टानि भद्रं ते भ्रातरं द्रक्ष्यसे तत:।।1.46.14।।
46.e: O the best of the brave ten years is yet to go (for completion of austerities). You will  have a brother. May you prosper

46.sa: तमहं त्वत्कृते पुत्र समाधास्ये जयोत्सुकम्। त्रैलोक्यविजयं पुत्र सह भोक्ष्यसि विज्वर:।।1.46.15।।
46.e: O Child I'll create in him eagerness victory. Together with him you will gain victory over the three worlds. Relieved of sorrows, enjoy you'll with him".

46.sa: एवमुक्त्वा दितिश्शक्रं प्राप्ते मध्यं दिवाकरे। निद्रयाऽपहृता देवी पादौ कृत्वाऽथ शीर्षत:।।1.46.16।।
46.e: After speaking thus to Indra, goddess Diti overpowered with sleep around midsday dropped off, her feet towards her head.

46.sa: दृष्ट्वा तामशुचिं शक्र: पादत: कृतमूर्धजाम्। शिरस्स्थाने कृतौ पादौ जहास च मुमोद च।।1.46.17।।
46.e: Indra laughed. He rejoiced at the sight of her ominous posture of sleeping with her feet towards her head and her hair falling on her feet.

46.sa: तस्याश्शरीरविवरं विवेश च पुरन्दर:। गर्भं च सप्तधा राम बिभेद परमात्मवान्।।1.46.18।।
46.e: O Rama with great courage Indra entered her womb and severed her embryo into  seven pieces.

46.sa: भिद्यमानस्ततो गर्भो वज्रेण शतपर्वणा। रुरोद सुस्वरं राम ततो दितिरबुध्यत।।1.46.19।।
46.e: O Rama that embryo, being severed by Vajra having a hundred edges, cried at high pitch which awakened Diti".

46.sa: मा रुदो मा रुदश्चेति गर्भं शक्रोऽभ्यभाषत। बिभेद च महातेजा रुदन्तमपि वासव:।।1.46.20।।
46.e: Highly powerful Indra, even while saying to the crying embryo  "Do not weep, Do not weep" severed it.

46.sa: न हन्तव्यो न हन्तव्य इत्येवं दितिरब्रवीत्। निष्पपात ततश्शक्रो मातुर्वचनगौरवात्।।1.46.21।।
46.e: "Do not kill", "Do not kill", said Diti. Subsequently Indra, in deference to the words of his mother, emerged out of the womb.

46.sa: प्राञ्जलिर्वज्रसहितो दितिं शक्रोऽभ्यभाषत। अशुचिर्देवि सुप्ताऽसि पादयो: कृतमूर्धजा।।1.46.22।।
46.e: Armed with Vajra, Indra addressed Diti with folded palms, saying, "O Devi you have slept,  with your head towards your feet and your hair falling on your feet".

46.sa: तदन्तरमहं लब्ध्वा शक्रहन्तारमाहवे। अभिदं सप्तधा देवि तन्मे त्वं क्षन्तुमर्हसि।।1.46.23।।
46.e: "I have seized the opportunity and severed into seven pieces the foetus who would have been a slayer of Indra. O Devi shoudn't you forgive me"? इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे षट्चत्वारिंशस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the fortysixth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

47.sa: सप्तधातु कृते गर्भे दिति: परमदु:खिता। सहस्राक्षं दुराधर्षं वाक्यं सानुनयाऽब्रवीत्।।1.47.1।।
47.e: Deeply distressed Diti, having come to know that the embryo had been severed into seven pieces, humbly spoke to the unassailable Indra.

47.sa: ममापराधाद्गर्भोऽयं सप्तधा विफलीकृत:। नापराधोऽस्ति देवेश तवात्र बलसूदन।।1.47.2।।
47.e: "O Indra, Slayer of Balasura, because of my fault this embryo has been made into seven pieces and rendered useless. In this matter you have not committed any fault.

47.sa: प्रियं तु कर्तुमिच्छामि मम गर्भविपर्यये। मरुतां सप्तसप्तानां स्थानपाला भवन्त्विमे।।1.47.3।।
47.e: This disaster to the embryo has happened contrary to expectations. Hence, I seek a favour from you. Let these seven pieces become seven guardians of marut regions (regions of the wind).

47.sa: वातस्कन्धा: इमे सप्त चरन्तु दिवि पुत्रक । मारुता इति विख्याता दिव्यरूपा ममात्मजा:।।1.47.4।।
47.e: O Son, all these seven are my sons of celestial beauty.They will become pesiding deities for Vata Skandha (divisions of wind) and let them be wellknown as maruts wandering in the universe.

47.sa: ब्रह्मलोकं चरत्वेक इन्द्रलोकं तथाऽपर:। दिवि वायुरिति ख्यातस्तृतीयोऽपि महायशा:।।1.47.5।।
47.e: Among them, one will move about in Brahmaloka, another in Indraloka, and the third, well known as vayu will move around in the sky.

47.sa: चत्वारस्तु सुरश्रेष्ठ दिशो वै तव शासनात्। सञ्चरिष्यन्तु भद्रं ते देवभूता ममात्मजा:।।1.47.6।।
47.e: O best of devatas by your command the other four sons will remain celestial, and will range about in four directions.

47.sa: तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सहस्राक्ष: पुरन्दर:। उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं दितिं बलनिषूदन:।।1.47.7।।
47.e: The thousandeyed Indra, slayer of Bala, on hearing Diti's words, addressed her with folded palms, saying:

47.sa: सर्वमेतद्यथोक्तं ते भविष्यति न संशय:। विचरिष्यन्ति भद्रं ते देवभूतास्तवात्मजा:।।1.47.8।।
47.e: "Everything will, no doubt, happen the way you said. Your sons will wander about as celestial beings. Prosperity to you."

47.sa: एवं तौ निश्चयं कृत्वा मातापुत्रौ तपोवने। जग्मतुस्त्रिदिवं राम कृतार्थाविति नश्श्रुतम्।।1.47.9।।
47.e: "O Rama mother and sons having arrived at this conclusion in the tapovana  ascended to heaven with their desire fulfilled. This is what we have heard."

47.sa: एष देशस्स काकुत्स्थ महेन्द्राध्युषित: पुरा। दितिं यत्र तपस्सिद्धामेवं परिचचार स:।।1.47.10।।
47.e: "O Descendant of Kakustha (Rama) this is that country which was formerly inhabited by Indra. Here Indra  attended on Diti who achieved the fruit of her austerities.

47.sa: इक्ष्वाकोऽस्तु नरव्याघ्र पुत्र: परमधार्मिक:।।1.47.11।। अलम्बुषायामुत्पन्नो विशाल इति विश्रुत:। तेन चासीदिह स्थाने विशालेति पुरी कृता।।1.47.12।।
47.e: "O Tiger among men (Rama) this highly virtuous and wellknown son named Vishala was born to Ikshvakus in Alambusa. Where, a city named Vishala was built.

47.sa: इक्ष्वाकोऽस्तु नरव्याघ्र पुत्र: परमधार्मिक:।।1.47.11।। अलम्बुषायामुत्पन्नो विशाल इति विश्रुत:। तेन चासीदिह स्थाने विशालेति पुरी कृता।।1.47.12।।
47.e: "O Tiger among men (Rama) this highly virtuous and wellknown son named Vishala was born to Ikshvakus in Alambusa. Where, a city named Vishala was built.

47.sa: विशालस्य सुतो राम हेमचन्द्रो महाबल:। सुचन्द्र इति विख्यात: हेमचन्द्रादनन्तर:।।1.47.13।।
47.e: O Rama mighty Hemachandra was Vishala's son. Hemachandra's successor was the celebrated Suchandra.

47.sa: सुचन्द्रतनयो राम धूम्राश्व इति विश्रुत:। धूम्राश्वतनयश्चापि सञ्जयस्समपद्यत।।1.47.14।।
47.e: O Rama son of Suchandra was Dhumraswa, wellknown Sanjaya was the son of Dhumraswa.

47.sa: सञ्जयस्य सुतश्श्रीमान् सहदेव: प्रतापवान्। कुशाश्वस्सहदेवस्य पुत्र: परमधार्मिक:।।1.47.15।।
47.e: Prosperous and powerful Sahadeva was Sanjaya's son. Highly virtuous Kusaswa was Sahadeva's son.

47.sa: कुशाश्वस्य महातेजा सोमदत्त: प्रतापवान्। सोमदत्तस्य पुत्रस्तु काकुत्स्थ इति विश्रुत:।।1.47.16।।
47.e: Brilliant and powerful Somadatta was Kusaswa's son. That Somadatta's son was Kakutstha is wellknown.

47.sa: तस्य पुत्रो महातेजा: सम्प्रत्येष पुरीमिमाम्। आवसत्यमरप्रख्यस्सुमतिर्नाम दुर्जय:।।1.47.17।।
47.e: Son of Ikshvakus, Sumati comparable to devatas, invincible and exceedingly energetic is still ruling this city.

47.sa: इक्ष्वाकोस्तु प्रसादेन सर्वे वैशालिका नृपा:। दीर्घायुषो महात्मानो वीर्यवन्तस्सुधार्मिका:।।1.47.18।।
47.e: By the grace of the Ikshvakus, all the kings of Vishala have been long lived and exalted, valiant and deeply religious.

47.sa: इहाद्य रजनीं राम सुखं वत्स्यामहे वयम्। श्व: प्रभाते नरश्रेष्ठ जनकं द्रष्टुमर्हसि।।1.47.19।।
47.e: O Rama we shall spend the right happily here. O Best among men On the tomorrow we see Janaka".

47.sa: सुमतिस्तु महातेजा विश्वामित्रमुपागतम्। श्रुत्वा नरवरश्रेष्ठ: प्रत्युद्गच्छन्महायशा:।।1.47.20।।
47.e: Having heard of the arrival of Viswamitra the celebrated Sumati, most brilliant chief of kings proceeded (to receive him).

47.sa: पूजां च परमां कृत्वा सोपाध्यायस्सबान्धव:। प्राञ्जलि: कुशलं पृष्ट्वा विश्वामित्रमथाब्रवीत्।।1.47.21।।
47.e: Along with his spiritual preceptors and relatives he paid Viswamitra great respect, enquired his wellbeing and said:

47.sa: धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि यस्य मे विषयं मुनि:। सम्प्राप्तो दर्शनं चैव नास्ति धन्यतरो मम।।1.47.22।।
47.e: "O Sage no one is more blessed than me since you have favoured me with your arrival in my country." इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे सप्तचत्वारिंशस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the fortyseventh sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

48.sa: पृष्ट्वा तु कुशलं तत्र परस्परसमागमे। कथान्ते सुमतिर्वाक्यं व्याजहार महामुनिम्।।1.48.1।।
48.e: Getting together they enquired one another's health. And then Sumati spoke to the great ascetic (Viswamitra).

48.sa: इमौ कुमारौ भद्रं ते देवतुल्यपराक्रमौ। गजसिंहगती वीरौ शार्दूलवृषभोपमौ।।1.48.2।। पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षौ खड्गतूणी धनुर्धरौ। अश्विनाविव रूपेण समुपस्थितयौवनौ।।1.48.3।। यदृच्छयैव गां प्राप्तौ देवलोकादिवामरौ। कथं पद्भ्यामिह प्राप्तौ किमर्थं कस्य वा मुने।।1.48.4।।
48.e: "O Sage, wish you well Who are these two youths who seem to possess the  prowess of celestial beings. They walk with the gait of an elephant or a lion. They are courageous like tiger or a bull. Their large eyes are like lotuspetals. They are armed with scimitars, bows and quivers. They are young and handsome like Aswinikumaras dropped from heaven casually. Whose sons are they? How did they  come here on foot? With what purpose?

48.sa: इमौ कुमारौ भद्रं ते देवतुल्यपराक्रमौ। गजसिंहगती वीरौ शार्दूलवृषभोपमौ।।1.48.2।। पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षौ खड्गतूणी धनुर्धरौ। अश्विनाविव रूपेण समुपस्थितयौवनौ।।1.48.3।। यदृच्छयैव गां प्राप्तौ देवलोकादिवामरौ। कथं पद्भ्यामिह प्राप्तौ किमर्थं कस्य वा मुने।।1.48.4।।
48.e: "O Sage, wish you well Who are these two youths who seem to possess the  prowess of celestial beings. They walk with the gait of an elephant or a lion. They are courageous like tiger or a bull. Their large eyes are like lotuspetals. They are armed with scimitars, bows and quivers. They are young and handsome like Aswinikumaras dropped from heaven casually. Whose sons are they? How did they  come here on foot? With what purpose?

48.sa: इमौ कुमारौ भद्रं ते देवतुल्यपराक्रमौ। गजसिंहगती वीरौ शार्दूलवृषभोपमौ।।1.48.2।। पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षौ खड्गतूणी धनुर्धरौ। अश्विनाविव रूपेण समुपस्थितयौवनौ।।1.48.3।। यदृच्छयैव गां प्राप्तौ देवलोकादिवामरौ। कथं पद्भ्यामिह प्राप्तौ किमर्थं कस्य वा मुने।।1.48.4।।
48.e: "O Sage, wish you well Who are these two youths who seem to possess the  prowess of celestial beings. They walk with the gait of an elephant or a lion. They are courageous like tiger or a bull. Their large eyes are like lotuspetals. They are armed with scimitars, bows and quivers. They are young and handsome like Aswinikumaras dropped from heaven casually. Whose sons are they? How did they  come here on foot? With what purpose?

48.sa: भूषयन्ताविमं देशं चन्द्रसूर्याविवाम्बरम्। परस्परस्य सदृशौ प्रमाणेङ्गितचेष्टितै:।।1.48.5।। किमर्थं च मुनिश्रेष्ठ सम्प्राप्तौ दुर्गमे पथि। वरायुधधरौ वीरौ श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वत:।।1.48.6।।
48.e: O Great ascetic they resemble each other in personality, expression and gestures. They adorn this land like Sun and moon in the sky holding excellent weapons. These heroes have trodden paths difficult to traverse. For what purpose have they come? I want to hear clearly".

48.sa: भूषयन्ताविमं देशं चन्द्रसूर्याविवाम्बरम्। परस्परस्य सदृशौ प्रमाणेङ्गितचेष्टितै:।।1.48.5।। किमर्थं च मुनिश्रेष्ठ सम्प्राप्तौ दुर्गमे पथि। वरायुधधरौ वीरौ श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वत:।।1.48.6।।
48.e: O Great ascetic they resemble each other in personality, expression and gestures. They adorn this land like Sun and moon in the sky holding excellent weapons. These heroes have trodden paths difficult to traverse. For what purpose have they come? I want to hear clearly".

48.sa: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा यथावृत्तं न्यवेदयत्। सिद्धाश्रमनिवासं च राक्षसानां वधं तथा।।1.48.7।।
48.e: On hearing his words, he (Viswamitra) related all about their stay at Siddhashrama and the slaying of rakshasas.

48.sa: विश्वामित्रवचश्श्रुत्वा राजा परमहर्षित:। अतिथी परमौ प्राप्तौ पुत्रौ दशरथस्य तौ।।1.48.8।। पूजयामास विधिवत्सत्कारार्हौ महाबलौ।
48.e: After hearing Viswamitra, the king (Sumati) got exceedingly delighted and extended hospitality in accordance with tradition to the highly valiant sons of Dasaratha, the distinguished guests worthy of honour.

48.sa: तत: परमसत्कारं सुमते: प्राप्य राघवौ।।1.48.9।। उष्य तत्र निशामेकां जग्मतुर्मिथिलां तत: ।
48.e: The descendants of Raghu (Rama and Lakshmana) having received great honour from Sumati, stayed there one night and thereafter set out for Mithila.

48.sa: तान् दृष्ट्वा मुनयस्सर्वे जनकस्य पुरीं शुभाम्।।1.48.10।। साधु साध्विति शंसन्तो मिथिलां समपूजयन्।
48.e: All the ascetics, having seen that auspicious city of Janaka worshipfully admired Mithila saying, 'Excellent, Excellent'

48.sa: मिथिलोपवने शून्यमाश्रमं दृश्य राघव:।।1.48.11।। पुराणं निर्जनं रम्यं पप्रच्छ मुनिपुङ्गवम्।
48.e: At the sight of an old uninhabited, beautiful and desolate hermitage in a grove near Mithila, the descendant of the Raghus enquired of the foremost among the ascetics (Viswamitra):

48.sa: श्रीमदाश्रमसङ्काशं किन्न्विदं मुनिवर्जितम्।।1.48.12।। ज्ञातुमिच्छामि भगवन् कस्यायं पूर्वमाश्रम:।
48.e: "O Venerable one I wish to know why this auspicios looking hermitage was deserted by ascetics? To whom did this belong in the past."

48.sa: तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवेणोक्तं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारद:।।1.48.13।। प्रत्युवाच महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महामुनि:।
48.e: Eloquent and brilliant Viswamitra, replied to the descendant of the Raghus saying:

48.sa: हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि श्रुणु तत्त्वेन राघव।।1.48.14।। यस्येदमाश्रमपदं शप्तं कोपान्महात्मना।
48.e: "O Descendant of the Raghus I shall tell all you about this hermitage cursed by the wrath of a great man.

48.sa: गौतमस्य नरश्रेष्ठ पूर्वमासीन्महात्मन:।।1.48.15।। आश्रमो दिव्यसङ्काशस्सुरैरपि सुपूजित:।
48.e: O Best among men this hermitage resembling a celestial retreat and wellhonoured even by devatas  once belonged to illustrious Gautama.

48.sa: स चेह तप आतिष्ठदहल्यासहित: पुरा।।1.48.16।। वर्षपूगाननेकांश्च राजपुत्र महायश:।
48.e: O Highly renowned prince it was here in ancient times that Gautama in the company of Ahalya practised austerities for several years.

48.sa: तस्यान्तरं विदित्वा तु सहस्राक्षश्शचीपति:।।1.48.17।। मुनिवेषधरोऽहल्यामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।
48.e: The thousandeyed Indra, consort of Sachi, having found an opportunity (during the absence of the ascetic), assumed the guise of the ascetic (Gautama) and said to Ahalya:

48.sa: ऋतुकालं प्रतीक्षन्ते नार्थिनस्सुसमाहिते।1.48.18 सङ्गमं त्वहमिच्छामि त्वया सह सुमध्यमे।।
48.e: 'O most beautiful one those overtaken by passion would not await the completion of the menstrual period (favourable for copulation). O woman of fine waist I desire union with you.'

48.sa: मुनिवेषं सहस्राक्षं विज्ञाय रघुनन्दन।1.48.19 मतिं चकार दुर्मेधा देवराजकुतूहलात्।।
48.e: O Delight of the Raghus the evilintentioned Ahalya, inclined towards the king of the celestials and  knowing him to be the thousandeyed Indra in the guise of the ascetic, consented for the union.

48.sa: अथाब्रवीत् नरश्रेष्ठ कृतार्थेनान्तरात्मना।1.48.20।। कृतार्थाऽस्मि सुरश्रेष्ठ गच्छ शीघ्रमित: प्रभो। आत्मानं मां च देवेश सर्वदा रक्ष गौतमात्।1.48.21।।
48.e: O Foremost of men with her heart's desire fulfilled, Ahalya said: "O Chief of the celestials I'm satisfied. O Lord, quit this place: O Lord of cthe gods, protect yourself and also me from Gautama in all respects."

48.sa: अथाब्रवीत् नरश्रेष्ठ कृतार्थेनान्तरात्मना।1.48.20।। कृतार्थाऽस्मि सुरश्रेष्ठ गच्छ शीघ्रमित: प्रभो। आत्मानं मां च देवेश सर्वदा रक्ष गौतमात्।1.48.21।।
48.e: O Foremost of men with her heart's desire fulfilled, Ahalya said: "O Chief of the celestials I'm satisfied. O Lord, quit this place: O Lord of cthe gods, protect yourself and also me from Gautama in all respects."

48.sa: इन्द्रस्तु प्रहसन् वाक्यमहल्यामिदमब्रवीत्। सुश्रोणि परितुष्टोऽस्मि गमिष्यामि यथाऽगतम्।1.48.22।।
48.e: Indra smilingly said to Ahalya, 'O One with lovely hips, I am  gratified. I shall go away the way I have come'.

48.sa: एवं सङ्गम्य तु तया निश्चक्रामोटजात्तत:।। स सम्भ्रमात्त्वरन् राम शङ्कितो गौतमं प्रति।1.48.23।।
48.e: O Rama he (Indra) came out of the leafhut quickly after his union with her, apprehensive of Gautama.

48.sa: गौतमं तं ददर्शाथ प्रविशन्तं महामुनिम्। देवदानवदुर्धर्षं तपोबलसमन्वितम्।।1.48.24।। तीर्थेंदकपरिक्लिन्नं दीप्यमानमिवानलम्। गृहीतसमिधं तत्र सकुशं मुनिपुङ्गवम्।।1.48.25।।
48.e: Subsequently, Indra beheld the great ascetic Gautama, unassailable by devatas and danavas, endowed with the power of ascetism, drenched with sacrifical waters,  shining like flaming fire, carrying sacrificial firewood and Kusha grass and preeminent  among sages, entering that leaf hut.

48.sa: गौतमं तं ददर्शाथ प्रविशन्तं महामुनिम्। देवदानवदुर्धर्षं तपोबलसमन्वितम्।।1.48.24।। तीर्थेंदकपरिक्लिन्नं दीप्यमानमिवानलम्। गृहीतसमिधं तत्र सकुशं मुनिपुङ्गवम्।।1.48.25।।
48.e: Subsequently, Indra beheld the great ascetic Gautama, unassailable by devatas and danavas, endowed with the power of ascetism, drenched with sacrifical waters,  shining like flaming fire, carrying sacrificial firewood and Kusha grass and preeminent  among sages, entering that leaf hut.

48.sa: दृष्ट्वा सुरपतिस्त्रस्तो विवर्णवदनोऽभवत्। अथ दृष्ट्वा सहस्राक्षं मुनिवेषधरं मुनि:।।1.48.26।। दुर्वृत्तं वृत्तसम्पन्नो रोषाद्वचनमब्रवीत्।
48.e: On seeing him, the face of the Lord of the gods (Indra) turned pale with fear. Having seen the wicked Indra with a thousandeyed in the guise of an ascetic the gentle sage Gautama got enraged and said:

48.sa: मम रूपं समास्थाय कृतवानसि दुर्मते।।1.48.27।। अकर्तव्यमिदं तस्माद्विफलस्त्वं भविष्यसि।
48.e: "O Wicked natured one assuming my form you have done a forbidden act. For that reason you shall be devoid of  scrotum.

48.sa: गौतमेनैवमुक्तस्य सरोषेण महात्मना।।1.48.28।। पेततुर्वृषणै भूमौ सहस्राक्षस्य तत्क्षणात्।
48.e: Cursed thus out of anger by eminent Gautama the  testicles of Indra immediately dropped down on the earth.

48.sa: तथा शप्त्वा स वै शक्रमहल्यामपि शप्तवान्।।1.48.29।। इह वर्षसहस्राणि बहूनि त्वं निवत्स्यसि। वायुभक्षा निराहारा तप्यन्ती भस्मशायिनी।।1.48.30।। अदृश्या सर्वभूतानां आश्रमेऽस्मिन्निवत्स्यसि।
48.e: Having thus cursed Indra, he also cursed Ahalya: 'You will be staying here for thousands of years without food and subsisting on air, lying down in ashes, doing penance, without being seen by any living beings in this ashrama'.

48.sa: तथा शप्त्वा स वै शक्रमहल्यामपि शप्तवान्।।1.48.29।। इह वर्षसहस्राणि बहूनि त्वं निवत्स्यसि। वायुभक्षा निराहारा तप्यन्ती भस्मशायिनी।।1.48.30।। अदृश्या सर्वभूतानां आश्रमेऽस्मिन्निवत्स्यसि।
48.e: Having thus cursed Indra, he also cursed Ahalya: 'You will be staying here for thousands of years without food and subsisting on air, lying down in ashes, doing penance, without being seen by any living beings in this ashrama'.

48.sa: यदा चैतद्वनं घोरं रामो दशरथात्मज:।।1.48.31।। आगमिष्यति दुर्धर्षस्तदा पूता भविष्यसि।
48.e: 'When the son of Dasaratha, the unassailable Rama enters this dreadful forest, you will be cleansed (of this sin)'.

48.sa: तस्यातिथ्येन दुर्वुत्ते लोभमोहविवर्जिता।।1.48.32।। मत्सकाशे मुदा युक्ता स्वं वपुर्धारयिष्यसि।
48.e: 'O Wickednatured one by offering hospitality to Rama, without covetousness and passion, you will happily live with me by regaining your present form'.

48.sa: एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा गौतमो दुष्टचारिणीम्।।1.48.33।। इममाश्रममुत्सृज्य सिद्धचारणसेविते। हिमवच्छिखरे पुण्ये तपस्तेपे महातपा:।।1.48.34।।
48.e: "Highly powerful Gautama who had performed rigid austerities thus cursed the wicked Ahalya and left this hermitage, for the peaks of Himavat mountain served by siddhas and charanas. Here he performed austerities"(said Viswamitra). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे अष्टचत्वारिंशस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the fortyeighth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

49.sa: अफलस्तु ततश्शक्रो देवानग्निपुरोगमान्। अब्रवीत्त्रस्तवदनस्सर्षिस्सङ्घान् सचारणान्।।1.49.1।।
49.e: Deprived of testicles, Indra with a frightened face addressed hordes of rishis and charanas with agni in the forefront.

49.sa: कुर्वता तपसो विघ्नं गौतमस्य महात्मन:। क्रोधमुत्पाद्य हि मया सुरकार्यमिदं कृतम्।।1.49.2।।
49.e: 'I have accomplished the objective of the devatas by creating obstacles to Gautama's  austerities, evoking in consequence the wrath of the magnanimous sage'.

49.sa: अफलोऽस्मि कृतस्तेन क्रोधात्सा च निराकृता। शापमोक्षेण महता तपोऽस्यापहृतं मया।।1.49.3।।
49.e: 'By his (Gautama's) wrath I have been deprived of my testicles. She (Ahalya) has  been deserted by him. He has lost his ascetic energy through the pronouncement of this great curse'.

49.sa: तस्मात्सुरवरास्सर्वे सर्षिस्सङ्घास्सचारणा: । सुरसाह्यकरं सर्वे सफलं कर्तुमर्हथ।।1.49.4।।
49.e: 'For that reason, O rishis, charanas and great devatas it is your duty to restore my testicles for the benefit I have given you'.

49.sa: शतक्रतोर्वचश्श्रुत्वा देवास्साग्निपुरोगमा:। पितृदेवानुपेत्याहु स्सह सर्वैर्मरुद्गणै:।।1.49.5।।
49.e: 'Hearing Indra, all the devatas accompanied by maruts. Lead by the Firegod devatas approached and said':

49.sa: अयं मेषस्सवृषणश्शक्रो ह्यवृषण: कृत:। मेषस्य वृषणौ गृह्य शक्रायाऽशु प्रयच्छथ।।1.49.6।।
49.e: 'This ram (which has received the share of your sacrificial offerings) has testicles. As Indra has been deprived of his own take these testicles immediately and graft them on to Indra'.

49.sa: अफलस्तु कृतो मेष: परां तुष्टिं प्रदास्यति। भवतां हर्षणार्थाय ये च दास्यन्ति मानवा:।।1.49.7।।
अग्नेस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा पितृदेवास्समागता:। उत्पाट्य मेषवृषणौ सहस्राक्षे न्यवेशयन्।।1.49.8।।
49.e: Hearing the words of the Firegod the pitrudevatas assembled, uprooted the testicles of the ram and grafted them on to Indra.

49.sa: तदा प्रभृति काकुत्स्थ पितृदेवास्समागता:। अफलान् भुञ्जते मेषान् फलैस्तेषामयोजयन्।।1.49.9।।
49.e: "O Son of the Kakutsthas from then on the pitrudevatas have been accepting rams  without testicles as offerings in a sacrifice, with ram's testicles fitted on to Indra.

49.sa: इन्द्रस्तु मेषवृषणस्तदाप्रभृति राघव। गौतमस्य प्रभावेन तपसश्च महात्मन:।।1.49.10।।
49.e: O Son of the Raghus illustrious Gautama's power of ascetism was such that thenceforth Indra possessed the testicles of a ram.

49.sa: तदागच्छ महातेज आश्रमं पुण्यकर्मण:। तारयैनां महाभागामहल्यां देवरूपिणीम्।।1.49.11।।
49.e: "Most brilliant Rama therefore enter the hermitage of the pious (Gautama) and liberate  this fortunate Ahalya of divine appearance (from the curse)."

49.sa: विश्वामित्रवचश्श्रुत्वा राघवस्सहलक्ष्मण:। विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य तमाश्रममथाविशत्।।1.49.12।।
49.e: In response to the words of Viswamitra Rama and Lakshmana entered the  hermitage, Viswamitra in front.

49.sa: ददर्श च महाभागां तपसा द्योतितप्रभाम्। लोकैरपि समागम्य दुर्निरीक्ष्यां सुरासुरै:।।1.49.13।। प्रयत्नान्निर्मितां धात्रा दिव्यां मायामयीमिव। स तुषारावृतां साभ्रां पूर्णचन्द्रप्रभामिव।।1.49.14।। मध्येंऽभसो दुराधर्षां दीप्तां सूर्यप्रभामिव।
49.e: Rama beheld the highly fortunate Ahalya, shining brilliantly with the power of her asceticism. She could not be seen even by men, suras or asuras joined together. She looked  divine and illusory as if created with special efforts by Brahma. Though not clearly visible, she was shining bright like the light of the full Moon muffled by mists in the sky and like the inviolable light of the Sun reflected in the water.

49.sa: ददर्श च महाभागां तपसा द्योतितप्रभाम्। लोकैरपि समागम्य दुर्निरीक्ष्यां सुरासुरै:।।1.49.13।। प्रयत्नान्निर्मितां धात्रा दिव्यां मायामयीमिव। स तुषारावृतां साभ्रां पूर्णचन्द्रप्रभामिव।।1.49.14।। मध्येंऽभसो दुराधर्षां दीप्तां सूर्यप्रभामिव।
49.e: Rama beheld the highly fortunate Ahalya, shining brilliantly with the power of her asceticism. She could not be seen even by men, suras or asuras joined together. She looked  divine and illusory as if created with special efforts by Brahma. Though not clearly visible, she was shining bright like the light of the full Moon muffled by mists in the sky and like the inviolable light of the Sun reflected in the water.

49.sa: सा हि गौतमवाक्येन दुर्निरीक्ष्या बभूव ह।।1.49.15।। त्रयाणामपि लोकानां यावद्रामस्य दर्शनम्।
49.e: By the words of Gautama, she became invisible to the three worlds till the appearance of Rama.

49.sa: शापस्यान्तमुपागम्य तेषां दर्शनमागता।।1.49.16।। राघवौ तु ततस्तस्या: पादौ जगृहतुस्तदा।
49.e: With the expiry of the period of the curse, the Raghavas (Rama and Lakshmana) speared and she became perceptible when Rama touched her feet.

49.sa: स्मरन्ती गौतमवच: प्रतिजग्राह सा च तौ।।1.49.17।। पाद्यमर्घ्यं तथाऽऽतिथ्यं चकार सुसमाहिता। प्रतिजग्राह काकुत्स्थो विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा।।1.49.18।।
49.e: Recalling the words of Gautama, she received them with water to wash their feet and offerings made with due devotion Rama accepted her hospitality extended in accordance tradition.

49.sa: स्मरन्ती गौतमवच: प्रतिजग्राह सा च तौ।।1.49.17।। पाद्यमर्घ्यं तथाऽऽतिथ्यं चकार सुसमाहिता। प्रतिजग्राह काकुत्स्थो विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा।।1.49.18।।
49.e: Recalling the words of Gautama, she received them with water to wash their feet and offerings made with due devotion Rama accepted her hospitality extended in accordance tradition.

49.sa: पुष्पवृष्टिर्महत्यासीद्देवदुन्दुभिनिस्वनै:। गन्धर्वाप्सरसां चैव महानासीत्समागम:।।1.49.19।।
49.e: Amidst sounds of celestial kettledrums, devatas showered flowers, gandharvas sang and apsarasa danced. There was a great assemblage (of divinities).

49.sa: साधु साध्विति देवास्तामहल्यां समपूजयन्। तपोबलविशुद्धाङ्गी गौतमस्य वशानुगाम्।।1.49.20।।
49.e: On seeing Ahalya, her body purified by the power of penance at Gautama's command, the devatas worshipfully exclaimed, 'Excellent, Excellent'

49.sa: गौतमोऽपि महातेजा अहल्यासहितस्सुखी। रामं सम्पूज्य विधिवत्तपस्तेपे महातपा:।।1.49.21।।
49.e: Brilliant Gautam, the great ascetic, along with Ahalya, worshipped Rama  according to tradition, with delight and continued with his austerities.

49.sa: रामोऽपि परमां पूजां गौतमस्य महामुने:। सकाशाद्विधिवत्प्राप्य जगाम मिथिलां तत:।।1.49.22।।
49.e: Having received due hospitality from the great ascetic Gautama Rama also set out towards Mithila. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे एकोनपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortyninth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

50.sa: तत: प्रागुत्तरां गत्वा रामस्सौमित्रिणा सह। विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य यज्ञवाटमुपागमत्।।1.50.1।।
50.e: Rama accompanied by Lakshmana with Viswamitra ahead proceeded in northeasterly direction and reached the sacrificial ground.

50.sa: रामस्तु मुनिशार्दूलमुवाच सहलक्ष्मण:। साध्वी यज्ञसमृद्धिर्हि जनकस्य महात्मन:।।1.50.2।।
50.e: Rama with Lakshmana told the tiger among ascetics Viswamitra that the preparations or the sacrifice by the illustrious king Janaka were excellent.

50.sa: बहूनीह सहस्राणि नानादेशनिवासिनाम्। ब्राह्मणानां महाभाग वेदाध्ययनशालिनाम्।।1.50.3।। ऋषिवाटाश्च दृश्यन्ते शकटीशतसङ्कुला:। देशो विधीयतां ब्रह्मन् यत्र वत्स्यामहे वयम्।।1.50.4।।
50.e: O Illustrious sage thousands of brahmins living in different countries and versed in  the study of the vedas have assembled here. The shelters for ascetics are thronged with hundreds of carts. O Great ascetic let us choose a place where we can stay.

50.sa: बहूनीह सहस्राणि नानादेशनिवासिनाम्। ब्राह्मणानां महाभाग वेदाध्ययनशालिनाम्।।1.50.3।। ऋषिवाटाश्च दृश्यन्ते शकटीशतसङ्कुला:। देशो विधीयतां ब्रह्मन् यत्र वत्स्यामहे वयम्।।1.50.4।।
50.e: O Illustrious sage thousands of brahmins living in different countries and versed in  the study of the vedas have assembled here. The shelters for ascetics are thronged with hundreds of carts. O Great ascetic let us choose a place where we can stay.

50.sa: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो महामुनि:। निवेशमकरोद्देशे विविक्ते सलिलायुते।।1.50.5।।
50.e: Great ascetic Viswamitra, hearing Rama's words, chose a nottoocrowded place near a watersource for encampment.

50.sa: विश्वामित्रमनुप्राप्तं श्रुत्वा स नृपतिस्तदा। शतानन्दं पुरस्कृत्य पुरोहितमनिन्दितम्।।1.50.6।। प्रत्युज्जगाम सहसा विनयेन समन्वित:।
50.e: When the king heard of the arrival of Viswamitra he went forward with Satananda, the blemishless family priest walking ahead in order to welcome him with humility.

50.sa: ऋत्विजोऽपि महात्मानस्त्वर्घ्यमादाय सत्वरम्।।1.50.7।। विश्वामित्राय धर्मेण ददुर्मंन्त्रपुरस्कृतम्।
50.e: Eminent officiating priests speedily brought the offerings of worship and paid obeisance to Viswamitra with prayers.

50.sa: प्रतिगृह्य च तां पूजां जनकस्य महात्मन:।।1.50.8।। पप्रच्छ कुशलं राज्ञो यज्ञस्य च निरामयम्।
50.e: Viswamitra received illustrious king Janaka's worship and enquired about the welfare of the king and the conduct of the sacrifice.

50.sa: स तांश्चापि मुनीन् पृष्ट्वा सोपाध्यायपुरोधस:।।1.50.9।। यथान्यायं ततस्सर्वैस्समागच्छत्प्रहृष्टवत्।
50.e: Viswamitra duly enquired the wellbeing of the sages and the spiritual teachers, priests in right order. And thereafter the rest joined them in great delight.

50.sa: अथ राजा मुनिश्रेष्ठं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत।।1.50.10।। आसने भगवानास्तां सहैभिर्मुनिपुङ्गवै:।
50.e: The king then folded his hands in supplication to the foremost of ascetics, Viswamitra, saying "O Venerable one please be seated along with the eminent ascetics."

50.sa: जनकस्य वचश्श्रुत्वा निषसाद महामुनि:।।1.50.11।। पुरोधा ऋत्विजश्चैव राजा च सह मन्त्रिभि:।
50.e: In response to Janaka's words, great sage Viswamitra occupied his seat. Thereafter the family priests, officiationg priests of the sacrifice, counsellors and also the king occupied their seats according to their rank.

50.sa: आसनेषु यथान्यायमुपविष्टान् समन्तत:।।1.50.12।। दृष्ट्वा स नृपतिस्तत्र विश्वामित्रमथाब्रवीत्।
50.e: Thereafter the king looked on all sides and  saw all of them seated  according to their rank and addressed Viswamitra saying:

50.sa: अद्य यज्ञसमृध्दिर्मे सफला दैवतै: कृता।।1.50.13।। अद्य यज्ञफलं प्राप्तं भगवद्दर्शनान्मया।
50.e: "Today my sacrifice has been rendered fruitful by the devatas. I have reaped the fruit of my sacrifice today by your venerable presence.

50.sa: धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि यस्य मे मुनिपुङ्गव।।1.50.14।। यज्ञोपसदनं ब्रह्मन् प्राप्तोऽसि मुनिभि: सह।
50.e: O Preeminent among ascetics O brahmana you have come to my sacrificial mandap along with these ascetics Blessed am I Obliged am I.

50.sa: द्वादशाहं तु ब्रह्मर्षे शेषमाहुर्मनीषिण:।।1.50.15।। ततो भागार्थिनो देवान् द्रष्टुमर्हसि कौशिक।
50.e: O Brahmarshi learned men say, only twelve days remain for completion of this acrifice. Thereafter O Viswamitra you should see devatas claiming their shares".

50.sa: इत्युक्त्वा मुनिशार्दूलं प्रहृष्टवदनस्तदा।।1.50.16।। पुनस्तं परिपप्रच्छ प्राञ्जलि: प्रणतो नृप:।
50.e: Having said this, the king (Janaka) with a cheerful countenance and saluting with folded palms again asked that tiger among ascetics (Viswamitra):

50.sa: इमौ कुमारौ भद्रं ते देवतुल्यपराक्रमौ।।1.50.17।। गजसिंहगती वीरौ शार्दूलवृषभोपमौ। पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षौ खड्गतूणीधनुर्धरौ।।1.50.18।। अश्विनाविव रूपेण समुपस्थितयौवनौ। यदृच्छयैव गां प्राप्तौ देवलोकादिवामरौ।।1.50.19।। कथं पद्भ्यामिह प्राप्तौ किमर्थं कस्य वा मुने।
50.e: "O Sage (Viswamitra), be blessed. Who are these two young men with the prowess of the celestials the gait of an elephant or a lion? They resemble a tiger or a bull in courage. They have large eyes like lotuspetals. They are armed with scimitars bows and quivers. With their approaching youth, they resemble the Aswinikumaras in beauty. They look like gods who have descended on earth from heaven out of their free will. Whose sons are they? How did they come here on foot? And for what purpose?

50.sa: इमौ कुमारौ भद्रं ते देवतुल्यपराक्रमौ।।1.50.17।। गजसिंहगती वीरौ शार्दूलवृषभोपमौ। पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षौ खड्गतूणीधनुर्धरौ।।1.50.18।। अश्विनाविव रूपेण समुपस्थितयौवनौ। यदृच्छयैव गां प्राप्तौ देवलोकादिवामरौ।।1.50.19।। कथं पद्भ्यामिह प्राप्तौ किमर्थं कस्य वा मुने।
50.e: "O Sage (Viswamitra), be blessed. Who are these two young men with the prowess of the celestials the gait of an elephant or a lion? They resemble a tiger or a bull in courage. They have large eyes like lotuspetals. They are armed with scimitars bows and quivers. With their approaching youth, they resemble the Aswinikumaras in beauty. They look like gods who have descended on earth from heaven out of their free will. Whose sons are they? How did they come here on foot? And for what purpose?

50.sa: इमौ कुमारौ भद्रं ते देवतुल्यपराक्रमौ।।1.50.17।। गजसिंहगती वीरौ शार्दूलवृषभोपमौ। पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षौ खड्गतूणीधनुर्धरौ।।1.50.18।। अश्विनाविव रूपेण समुपस्थितयौवनौ। यदृच्छयैव गां प्राप्तौ देवलोकादिवामरौ।।1.50.19।। कथं पद्भ्यामिह प्राप्तौ किमर्थं कस्य वा मुने।
50.e: "O Sage (Viswamitra), be blessed. Who are these two young men with the prowess of the celestials the gait of an elephant or a lion? They resemble a tiger or a bull in courage. They have large eyes like lotuspetals. They are armed with scimitars bows and quivers. With their approaching youth, they resemble the Aswinikumaras in beauty. They look like gods who have descended on earth from heaven out of their free will. Whose sons are they? How did they come here on foot? And for what purpose?

50.sa: वरायुधधरौ वीरौ कस्य पुत्रौ महामुने।।1.50.20।। भूषयन्ताविमं देशं चन्द्रसूर्याविवाम्बरम्। परस्परस्य सदृशौ प्रमाणेङ्गितचेष्टितै:।।1.50.21।। काकपक्षधरौ वीरौ श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वत:।
50.e: Great ascetic, these two young men with hair falling on their temples like the wings of a crow, each of them resemble the other in personality, expressions and gestures. Wielding excellent weapons they adorn this land like the Moon and the Sun deck the sky. Whose sons are they? I wish truly to hear about these heroes".

50.sa: वरायुधधरौ वीरौ कस्य पुत्रौ महामुने।।1.50.20।। भूषयन्ताविमं देशं चन्द्रसूर्याविवाम्बरम्। परस्परस्य सदृशौ प्रमाणेङ्गितचेष्टितै:।।1.50.21।। काकपक्षधरौ वीरौ श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वत:।
50.e: Great ascetic, these two young men with hair falling on their temples like the wings of a crow, each of them resemble the other in personality, expressions and gestures. Wielding excellent weapons they adorn this land like the Moon and the Sun deck the sky. Whose sons are they? I wish truly to hear about these heroes".

50.sa: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा जनकस्य महात्मन:।।1.50.22।। न्यवेदयन्महात्मानौ पुत्रौ दशरथस्य तौ।
50.e: Hearing the words of the magnanimous Janaka, Viswamitra presented them to him saying that they were the illustrious sons of Dasaratha.

50.sa: सिद्धाश्रमनिवासं च राक्षसानां वधं तथा।।1.50.23।। तच्चागमनमव्यग्रं विशालायाश्च दर्शनम्। अहल्यादर्शनं चैव गौतमेन समागमम्।।1.50.24।। महाधनुषि जिज्ञासां कर्तुमागमनं तथा। एतत्सर्वं महातेजा जनकाय महात्मने ।।1.50.25।। निवेद्य विररामाथ विश्वामित्रो महामुनि:।
50.e: The great ascetic Viswamitra, who was highly powerful related to the distinguished Janaka in full their undaunted journey to Siddhashrama and the slaughter of rakshasas there, the view of the city of Vishala, meeting with Ahalya and Gautama and the inquisitiveness about the great bow which brought them to Mithila and then kept quiet. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाणडे पञ्चाशस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the fiftieth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
